text.p: Commodities were generally weaker, with metals volatile and unpredictable, wheat hit by sharply lower soy, but gold and oil firmer.

Base metals were volatile and unpredictable. Copper and aluminium ended with pared losses, with copper recovering well from an early-afternoon decline that threatened to extend significantly lower. However, the backwardation narrowed markedly, which suggested that the downside of the current $2,330/2,370 range should be favoured, traders said. Prices briefly fell under $2,330, but bounced back to close the kerb at $2,338, still down $7 a tonne from Tuesday.

Aluminium made another foray towards the $1,700 target before the rise was squashed by tumbling copper prices. However, the solid physical undertone emanating from the U.S. restricted declines, and prices ended at $1,666, down $9.

Lead and zinc movements were wide throughout the session, with speculative interest driving prices higher before copper's downturn partially dampened sentiment. Nevertheless both markets were resilient on the dips and pushed higher on the kerb. Zinc, which hit a fresh 4-1/2 year peak of $1,279 at one stage, closed at $1,275, a gain of $24, while lead ended at $693, up $22 from the previous kerb.

Nickel trading was also variable, with prices fluctuating in line with copper's mood swings, before they trended upwards during the kerb. Traders said the market was supported on dips towards the $8,000 level, and by the end of the kerb three months was $40 higher at $8,070.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed to lower Wednesday on moderate volumes, with most CRB-index commodities down as funds took profits on seasonal rallies, analysts said. New York bullion was trading late at S$351.95 per ounce, up from the London fix of $351.40. "Precious metals have been a little bearish in recent days, after news of the Swiss plan to sell some gold, but Swiss National Bank chairman Meyer today again said no gold would be sold until 1999," said Jeff Kowal, a fund manager with Toronto-based Friedberg Mercantile Group. " overall commodities were down across the board today, and that may have rubbed off on precious metals also."

A sharp break in the soybean market, triggered by signs the U.S. may be importing soybeans from Brazil, pressed CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said. Selling was broad-based in late dealings amid the aggressive selloff in soybeans and the near limit losses in the corn pit, they said. heat was higher most of the session on talk Egypt was seeking 500,000 tonnes of wheat -- Australia was expected to contend for the business -- and on ideas that U.S. soft red winter wheat acreage could be reduced. Wheat closed 2-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with March down five at $3.76.

NYMEX crude closed higher on continued short covering after spot crude confirmed a key support area beneath $20.00 in the morning, traders said. April crude closed up 47 cents a barrel at $20.58 after rising as high as $20.85 and falling as low as $19.86. On March 3, prompt crude dropped to $19.96 but rebounded intraday. May closed at 20.65.
